key_insight: Surrogate-guided reinforcement learning enriches perovskite recipe shortlists with candidates near high-performing measured devices, without establishing experimental performance.
engineering_relevance: The framework could help prioritize solar-cell recipes for fabrication across a combinatorial space of compositions, device layers, and processing choices.
method: Generate recipes with reinforcement-learning policies guided by a frozen TabPFN surrogate.
Assess neighborhood support using a reference pool of 890 measured devices.
Compare three learned policies with six baselines using 3,000 surrogate evaluations per run.
evidence_signal: Five-fold evaluation on 1,846 devices raised mean PCE from 19.68% to 23.74% through top-ten selection; top-100 neighborhood-supported hit rates were 23% for PPO and 24% for recurrent PPO, versus 2.9% for Pure Random.
watch_item: Neighborhood support weakens at stricter similarity thresholds, and experimental gains, seed robustness, and matched-budget advantage remain unestablished.
paper_title: Enrichment-Oriented Virtual Screening of Perovskite Solar Cells through Reinforcement Learning
